cur:monumental-hagia-sophia-southwestern.summary: Against a gold ground in the lunette above the doorway, the Virgin sits on a backless jewelled throne with the Christ Child on her lap, who blesses and holds a scroll. Emperor Constantine, at her left, offers a model of the walled city of Constantinople, and Emperor Justinian, at her right, a model of Hagia Sophia itself. The two founders thus entrust city and church to the protection of the Mother of God and her Son.
facts: The mosaic dates from the reign of Basil II and was rediscovered during the restoration by the Fossati brothers in 1849.
The enthroned Virgin was probably modelled on the earlier mosaic in the apse semi-dome of the church.

cur:objects-otto-imperator-ivory-milan.summary: Christ sits enthroned between St Mary and St Maurice, raising his hands over a small imperial family who prostrate themselves at his feet: the emperor, the empress and a little crowned son. The inscription OTTO IMPERATOR runs along the base, and the letters IHS XPS name Christ above. The plaque expresses the Ottonian ideal of the emperor as the humble servant and representative of Christ the true King.
facts: The V&A notes that this relief of Christ enthroned with the Emperor Otto II, his wife and child is stylistically related to the Basilewsky Situla, suggesting both were made in Milan around 980.
The figures are usually identified as Otto II, Theophanu and the infant Otto III, though some have proposed Otto I and Adelaide.
cur:objects-otto-imperator-ivory-milan.notes: The flanking saints are identified by the inscriptions SCA MARIA and SCS MAURICIUS visible on the frame. Image is small (486 px).
